transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I… I guess I got scared. I keep having these thoughts that it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes, driving home from the clinic, I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just… didn’t turn the wheel.
Are you intending to kill yourself?
I… I don’t know if I’d say I’m intending to. But the thoughts are there. Like… not waking up, or when I’m driving, wondering what would happen if I just didn’t turn the wheel. That scared me.
Have you made a specific plan to kill yourself?
Not… not a plan exactly. It’s more like those thoughts — not wanting to wake up, or when I’m driving and I wonder what if I just didn’t turn the wheel. I haven’t sat down and planned it out.
Have you done anything to get ready to hurt yourself?
No… I don’t think I’ve done anything to get ready. It’s more… the thoughts that scared me. Like not waking up, or when I’m driving home and I wonder what would happen if I just didn’t turn the wheel.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… most days, honestly. It’s like everything just feels kind of drained out. Even when everyone’s around and the house is busy, I’ll go hide in the laundry room and cry because I don’t want anyone to see how… hopeless I feel.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah… I guess I have. I haven’t really touched my camera, or cared much about the bird feeders or what’s coming up in the garden. Those used to be… kind of how I felt like myself, so it’s scary.
Has there been a time in your life when you went through a similar period of feeling this depressed?
I’m… not sure. I mean, I’ve had low stretches before, I guess, but I don’t know if it was like this. I’d have to think about it.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally up or unusually energetic for several days in a row?

I guess… yes. Earlier this month there were a few days where I felt almost too upbeat, like wired. And then I’d snap at people over stupid little things at work, like a medication cup being in the wrong place or the morning schedule changing. It didn’t really feel like me.
During those upbeat, wired days, did you need less sleep than usual?
Yeah… I was sleeping maybe three hours a night, but I’d still wake up before sunrise feeling pretty sharp. Like I didn’t really need more.
During those upbeat, wired days, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could do things other people couldn't?
I don’t think so. Not powerful or anything like that. Maybe just… more sure of myself than usual, but I wouldn’t say I felt like I could do things other people couldn’t.
During those upbeat, wired days, were you more active than usual or starting lots of projects?

Yes… I was definitely more active. After work I couldn’t really sit still. I’d pace around the house, start measuring rooms, making lists, reorganizing cabinets… even late at night when everyone else was already in bed.
During those wired, upbeat days, were you talking more than usual or so fast that other people noticed?
I’m not sure… I don’t think anyone said I was talking too fast. Maybe I was a little more chatty, but I didn’t really notice.
During those wired, upbeat days, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive?

A little, I guess. I bought a bunch of things all at once… monitoring equipment, ramps, bedding, supplies. At the time it felt like we really needed it right then. Afterward I realized I’d put it on the credit card, and… we really can’t cover that.
About how many days in a row did that wired, upbeat period last?
It was several days in a row… I don’t remember the exact number. Long enough that after work I kept pacing around, measuring rooms and making lists, even after everyone else had gone to bed.
Did that wired, unusually upbeat period last at least 4 days in a row?
I… I’m not completely sure. It felt like several days, but I can’t say for certain it was four.
During that wired, upbeat period, were you hospitalized because of it?
No… I wasn’t hospitalized for it.
During those wired, upbeat days, did that change cause problems at work or at home?

Yes… it did. I’ve been making mistakes at the clinic, and at home my husband’s had to take over more—bills, meals, things like that. I’ve also pulled back from friends because I’m afraid I’ll snap or… just fall apart.
During those wired, upbeat days, did you feel driven to get a lot of things done or start lots of tasks?

Yes. I… took on too much. Extra shifts, reorganizing the whole house schedule, calling contractors. I was trying to coordinate everyone like it was some big project, even though nobody had asked me to.
During those wired, upbeat days, did you feel unusually important or more capable than other people?
I don’t think so. I mean… I felt like I could handle more than usual, maybe, but not like I was better than other people or especially important.
Thinking about that wired, unusually upbeat stretch earlier this month, did it last 4 days in a row?
I’m… not sure. I didn’t really track it that closely. It was several days, but I can’t say for certain it was four in a row.
